title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7

title: Stocks Edge Up as Korea Gains, Brent Crude Climbs: Markets Wrap
summary: Asian stocks gained Friday as traders looked past geopolitical tensions and technology stocks advanced in South Korea. Oil rose as prospects for a lasting Middle East agreement remained uncertain.

title: Mexico Arrests Ex-Governor Over 2014 Student Abduction Case
summary: Mexican authorities detained a former governor over charges he concealed evidence in the more than decade-old abduction and presumed murder of dozens of students training to be teachers, one of the country’s most infamous criminal cases.

title: Yen Surrenders Nearly Half Its Gains from US-Japan Intervention
summary: The yen is heading into the end of the week having surrendered nearly half of its intervention-driven gains, fueling speculation among traders that authorities may step into the market again.

title: Kirin Pushes Into Vitamin Sales With $1.4 Billion Jamieson Deal
summary: Kirin Holdings Co. shares rose 2.4% to near record levels after the Japanese beverage maker announced a deal to acquire Toronto-based Jamieson Wellness Inc. that values the Canadian vitamins and supplements maker at about C$2 billion ($1.4 billion).

title: Singapore's DBS CEO Sees AI Costs Falling in ‘Token Paradox’
summary: DBS Group CEO Tan Su Shan sees AI costs trending down with more use of tokens, driven by what she calls the 'paradox of token spend.' She emphasizes that the bank maintains an open architecture, staying open-minded and avoiding being 'too wedded' to a model or any one provider. In a wide-ranging interview with Bloomberg's Haslinda Amin, Tan also outlines key growth areas, highlighting Taiwan as the bank's most exciting market opportunity in the next two to three years. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Steady as Traders Assess Impact of Hormuz Flare-Up on Rates
summary: Gold moved in a narrow range as traders assessed the impact of a reported Iranian attack in the Strait of Hormuz on the Federal Reserve’s path for interest rates.

title: Fed's Musalem Expresses Preference to Raise Rates
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem explains why he expressed a preference to raise rates at the Federal Open Market Committee's July meeting. Speaking at an event in São Paulo, Musalem also discusses the outlook for inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed's Musalem Sees Need for 'Meaningful Restraint' on Inflation
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem says policymakers can't afford to tolerate higher inflation while they wait for the possibility of stronger productivity growth. He speaks at an event in São Paulo. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chinese Banks Expand Direct Settlement to Aid Yuan’s Global Role
summary: China is accelerating its push to internationalize the yuan as domestic banks add new foreign currencies available for direct settlement to bypass the dollar in cross-border trade.

title: Japan Sees Rush for Covenant Shelter as BBB-Rated Bond Sales Fly
summary: Japanese companies have already sold more corporate bonds with investor protection this year than in all of 2025, as lower-rated borrowers increasingly turn to the bond market instead of relying solely on bank loans for their funding needs.

title: Trex CEO on Earnings, Consumer Demand For Deck Materials
summary: Trex CEO Adam Zambanini joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the deck materials company's latest earnings results, the company's total addressable market, push into the Southern Sunbelt, customer demand, and more. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Japan Small Caps Face Survival Race as Topix Cull Looms
summary: Japan’s Topix stock index is poised for its biggest overhaul, with more than 600 companies — over a third of its constituents — likely to be gradually removed under new eligibility rules, according to analysts’ estimates.

title: Airbnb Lifts 2026 Outlook Again on US, European Demand
summary: Airbnb Inc. boosted its annual revenue forecast for a second time this year after it saw robust global travel demand, particularly in the US and Europe.

title: Big Take: The situation at Situational Awareness
summary: On today’s Big Take podcast, hedge fund reporters Katherine Burton and Hema Parmar join Sarah Holder to break down the rise of 24-year-old ‘Nostradamus of AI’ Leopold Aschenbrenner, the meltdown of his hedge fund Situational Awareness and whether the episode exposes broader hedge fund vulnerabilities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed’s Fima Repo Facility Went Unused for 8th Straight Week
summary: A rarely used Federal Reserve liquidity facility saw no activity last week, suggesting Japan didn’t use the tool in its latest effort to support the yen.

title: Follow the Money All the Way to Carney's Canada
summary: Bloomberg News Editor-in-Chief Emeritus Matt Winkler explains what is behind Canada's investment boom. The country's government poised to attract record investment from outside its borders after foreigners poured $183 billion into Canada’s stocks and bonds in the past year. Winkler says its thanks to "reasonable" policies, crediting Prime Minister Mark Carney -- a Rhodes Scholar, former Bank of Canada Governor, and former Bloomberg Board Chair -- for attracting investors to Canada by being "somebody the world knows very well." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Elanco CEO on Boosted Forecast, Surge in Tick Bites
summary: Elanco Animal Health President and CEO Jeff Simmons discusses what's behind the company's increased profit and revenue forecasts. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Simmons also comments on the recent surge in tick bites and consumer spending on pet health products. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AIG Profit Beat Estimates, Cites Strong Underwriting
summary: American International Group Inc. reported second-quarter results that surpassed Wall Street expectations, roughly two months after Eric Andersen took over as chief executive officer.

title: Elf Beauty Expands Into Hair Care Products
summary: Elf Beauty Chief Executive Officer Tarang Amin says the company is excited about expanding into hair care products. It launched a new partnership with Target in June. Amin talks about that and the latest earnings report on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
